test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: During each respiratory cycle, when air is inhaled and exhaled, there is always a certain amount of air in the lungs so that there is enough time to absorb oxygen and release carbon dioxide. What is this amount of air called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Residual amount**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The residual amount, also known as residual volume, is the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a maximal exhalation.
 
• It is crucial as it prevents the lungs from collapsing and ensures continuous gas exchange (oxygen and carbon dioxide) between breaths.
 
• This volume of air cannot be voluntarily exhaled, and it typically amounts to about 1200 ml in healthy adult males.
 
• Residual volume is essential for maintaining a consistent concentration of gases in the blood, even during different phases of the breathing cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Respiratory Cycle:**

 
 
• The respiratory cycle consists of inhalation and exhalation. During inhalation, air is drawn into the lungs, and during exhalation, air is expelled from the lungs.
 
• Efficient gas exchange occurs in the alveoli where oxygen from the inhaled air diffuses into the blood, and carbon dioxide from the blood diffuses into the alveoli to be exhaled.
 
 
 
• **Pulmonary Volume:**
 
 
• Various volumes of air are associated with breathing: tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume, expiratory reserve volume, and residual volume.
 
• Tidal volume is the amount of air inhaled or exhaled during a normal breath, typically around 500 ml in adults.
 
 
 
• **Alveolar Volume:**
 
 
• The alveolar volume refers to the volume of air in the alveoli that participates in gas exchange. This is a part of the tidal volume that reaches the alveoli and is available for gas exchange.
 
• Maintaining proper alveolar volume is essential for effective oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange.
